# Anatomy of Anthropic — The Philosophy, Products, Economics, and Governance Behind the World's Most Deliberate AI Company

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> dissecting Anthropic across six layers: origin (PBC / Long-Term Benefit
> Trust), philosophy (Constitutional AI / Mechanistic Interpretability),
> model architecture (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus), products (Claude Code /
> Cowork / MCP), economics (the Anthropic Economic Index), and governance
> (Responsible Scaling Policy). As stated in the book's conclusion:
> "Deliberateness generates trust. Trust generates adoption. Adoption
> generates disruptive power." Sequel to the author's "The Silence of
> Intelligence" (Industry Anatomy Series #2).

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/anatomy_of_anthropic_jp.md): 全6章・参考文献12件収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/anatomy_of_anthropic_en.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- Chapter 1: Anthropic was founded as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) in
  2021, governed by a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT) that holds the power to
  appoint the board of directors — a structure the book describes as making
  "safety-compromising decisions structurally difficult," in explicit
  contrast to OpenAI's transition from non-profit to capped-profit
- Chapter 2: The book states Claude's constitution has four core principles
  in a strict hierarchy — safety and human oversight first, ethical behavior
  second, Anthropic's guidelines third, and helpfulness to the user placed
  last
- Chapter 3: The book documents two occasions on which a mid-tier model
  surpassed the prior flagship — Claude 3.5 Sonnet over Claude 3 Opus
  (June 2024), and Claude Sonnet 4.6 over Opus 4.5 (Feb 2026, preferred by
  70% of developers over Sonnet 4.5 and 59% over Opus 4.5)
- Chapter 4: The book states Claude Code reached $1B in annual revenue
  within 6 months of general availability, and that the Cowork research
  preview was followed by roughly $285B in aggregate market-cap decline
  across enterprise software stocks (ServiceNow, Salesforce, Snowflake,
  Intuit, Thomson Reuters), with IBM falling 13.2% in a single day
- Chapter 4: MCP (Model Context Protocol) was donated to the Agentic AI
  Foundation under the Linux Foundation in Dec 2025, co-founded by
  Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI
- Chapter 5: The Anthropic Economic Index's January 2026 report found AI
  used in 25%+ of tasks in 49% of occupations (up from 36% in the first
  report), and its March 2026 labor market report found "no significant
  rise in unemployment" for high-AI-exposure occupations overall, but
  "suggestive evidence" of slowing hiring for workers aged 22–25 in those
  occupations
- Chapter 6: The book documents Anthropic's February 2026 refusal to grant
  the U.S. Department of Defense contractual guarantees against autonomous
  weapons and domestic surveillance use, followed by Claude reaching #1 on
  the App Store above ChatGPT in 16 countries
